title: Probably all organisms descend from one primordial form

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Probably all organisms descend from one primordial form

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: By analogy, probably all organisms that have ever lived on earth have descended from a single primordial form.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Therefore I should infer from analogy that probably all the organic beings which have ever lived on this earth have descended from some one primordial form, into which life was first breathed.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter XIV, “Recapitulation and Conclusion”; section “How far the theory of natural selection may be extended”. Scope: all organisms that have ever lived on earth

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch14-04: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.75

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Universal ancestry has explicit comparative-genomic predictions and massive public datasets. Exact singularity at life's origin remains inferential, but alternatives can be meaningfully discriminated with existing data.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Test universal common ancestry against multiple-origin models using conserved molecular machinery, near-universal genes, the genetic code and rare shared features while accounting for horizontal transfer. Strong likelihood or model-selection support for one connected ancestry supports the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The earliest signal is obscured by horizontal gene transfer and sequence saturation.

All organisms that ever lived cannot be sampled directly.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.78
data existence: 0.94
operationalizability: 0.7
analysis feasibility: 0.58
discriminating power: 0.68

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public genomes can strongly test common ancestry of extant life, which is the part of the claim that has measurable descendants. They cannot show that every organism that ever lived, including any vanished independent origin, belonged to that same genealogy. The analysis of universal genes is standard; the scope phrase 'which have ever lived' is why the claim is only partly resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Test whether all extant organisms, and fossils that can be placed, share homologous core genes and a single rooted network of descent. The claim is confirmed for known life if those cores are universal and congruent, and refuted if a lineage has an unrelated genetic system; organisms that left no descendants remain outside the test.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A second origin that died out without descendants would not appear in genomes or in the fossil record of later life.

Gene exchange at the root is compatible both with one primordial cell and with a community of exchanging forms.

Universal chemistry is expected under common ancestry and is also expected if early chemical options were severely limited.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.55
operationalizability: 0.7
data existence: 0.9
data adequacy: 0.6
analysis feasibility: 0.75
